summary:
Bauchi's Sharia Penal Code remains in force. The UK Home Office country policy and information note of June 2025 confirms it, and death by stoning is the penalty provided under Section 133 of the Bauchi Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 and Section 134 of the Bauchi State Penal Law of 2001.

On 28 June 2022 a Sharia court sitting in Ningi local government area sentenced three men to death by stoning for homosexuality, among them 70-year-old Malam Haruna. The prosecution was brought by members of the Hisbah Vanguard through Adamu Dan Kafi, who told the court the three were arrested at Gwada village, Ningi LGA, on 14 June 2022. Presiding judge Munka'ilu Sabo-Ningi held that they had violated Section 134 of the Bauchi State Penal Law of 2001 and granted a 30-day appeal window. Relatives of the convicted men said the judgment had not been carried out at the time of reporting. Reuters described the sentence as the first time the death penalty had actually been imposed for homosexuality in Nigeria.

The UK Home Office note records that the 2022 Bauchi sentence could not be carried out until ratified by the state governor, and that a further report placed a death-by-stoning sentence for homosexuality from a Sharia court in Bauchi in May 2024.

Earlier convictions in the state were reversed on appeal. Jubrin Babaji was convicted on 25 September 2003 under Section 133 of the Bauchi Sharia Penal Code Law 2001 and sentenced to death by stoning; the Upper Sharia Court of Bauchi State quashed the sentence for denial of counsel and a defective confession. Yunusa Rafin Chiyawa's conviction was quashed on 14 November 2003. Amnesty International recorded a number of cases in which convictions and sentences to death were quashed on appeal.

In 2007 Bauchi state police arrested eighteen men and charged them with sodomy for dressing as women, an offence under the Shari'a penal code. The charges were later reduced to vagrancy, and the men were held in jail for several years awaiting trial; the pre-trial detention dissolved by the end of 2011.

Persons perceived as trans-feminine in Bauchi have been arrested and held in custody under Shari'a charges for years.
tangentialFactors:
The 2022 Ningi sentence could not be carried out until ratified by the state governor, and relatives said it had not been carried out at the time of reporting. No stoning sentence in Bauchi is recorded as having been carried out.

At a sodomy trial in January 2014 at Bauchi's Tudun Alkali Upper Sharia Court, an angry mob stormed the premises demanding a death sentence.

The reversals recorded in Bauchi turned on procedural defects, denial of counsel and a defective confession, rather than on the lawfulness of the offence itself.
localsOnly:
Prosecutions in Bauchi's Sharia courts have been brought by the Hisbah Vanguard, a local morality-enforcement body, through individual complainants such as Adamu Dan Kafi in the Ningi case.

The 2007 arrests show charges reduced from sodomy to vagrancy while detention continued for years: the downgrade of a charge did not shorten custody.

For residents, the recorded pattern is arrest and prolonged pre-trial detention under Shari'a charges rather than concluded trials.
outOfScopeNotes:
The outcome of any appeal against the 2022 Ningi death-by-stoning sentence is not recorded in the sources reviewed.

Whether the death-by-stoning sentence reported from a Bauchi Sharia court in May 2024 was ratified by the state governor, or carried out, is not sourced.

No source records where detainees perceived as trans-feminine are housed inside Bauchi custody, whether in a male or female wing, a special unit, solitary confinement or segregation, and no trans-specific placement rule, facility or policy is documented for Bauchi.

The current status of the eighteen men arrested in 2007, after the dissolution of their pre-trial detention at the end of 2011, is not recorded.
